parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by ‘special educational need’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe the causes and effects of attention deficit hyperactive disorder (ADHD). 
Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have found out about learning and teaching styles.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
We know that students have different learning styles and that teachers have different teaching
styles, but there are different ways to measure these styles. Evaluate what psychologists
have found out about learning and teaching styles including a discussion of the methods used
to gather data. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline the main features of the humanistic approach to education.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Suggest how Eric can use the humanistic approach to prepare students for examinations.

text: You are meeting your friend Eric for the first time in several years. You know he believes in the
humanistic approach to education and you are looking forward to hearing all about it.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Suggest a behaviour modification technique that would help to control this attention-seeking
behaviour.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Explain the psychology on which your suggestion is based. 
Psychology and Health
Section A
Answer this question.

text: A child in your class is an attention-seeker. Every time you turn away she is out of her seat and
every time you talk to the class she interrupts. It is becoming a problem as it is disruptive to the
class.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by ‘accident proneness’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Using an example, describe the ‘illusion of invulnerability’ explanation of human error. 
Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have discovered about pain.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
“How can I get the doctor to understand how much pain I’m in?” Evaluate what psychologists
have discovered about pain and include a discussion of the usefulness of self reports. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the main features of Münchausen syndrome.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Suggest how data can be gathered on the behaviour of a person with Münchausen syndrome.

text: Münchausen syndrome derives from Baron Münchausen (1720–1797) who apparently told many
exaggerated anecdotes about himself. Asher applied the name to people who misuse health
services.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe one study which has used the ‘providing information’ technique.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Suggest a suitable health promotion campaign to encourage breast and testicular
self-examination. 
Psychology and Environment
Section A
Answer this question.

text: Imagine there are reports that breast and testicular cancer are on the increase. You have been
asked to devise a strategy to encourage people to examine themselves because it is known
that the discovery of a lump through self-examination significantly increases the chances of full
recovery.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by ‘personal space invasion’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe a study that has used the simulation method of measuring personal space. 
Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have found out about architecture and behaviour.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Environmental determinism, biological determinism and now architectural determinism!
Evaluate what psychologists have found out about architecture and include a discussion of
the issue of determinism. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe a laboratory experiment of how people behave in emergency situations.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Suggest how you would investigate how people behave in the emergency evacuation of an
aeroplane.

text: How do people behave when they escape from an aeroplane in an emergency? You decide to
investigate this for yourself, but you want to make the situation as true to real life as you can.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe one laboratory study and one non-laboratory study of animal crowding done by
psychologists.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Suggest how you would investigate the effect of spatial density on animals in a laboratory. 
Psychology and Abnormality
Section A
Answer this question.

text: There have been a number of studies investigating crowding in animals. You decide to conduct a
study of your own using an animal of your choice.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by the term ‘treating phobias’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe two ways in which phobias can be treated. 
Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have discovered about addiction and impulse control disorders.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
“No single explanation of impulse control disorders is adequate.” Evaluate what psychologists
have discovered about addiction and impulse control disorders and include a discussion
about competing explanations. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the main features of psychotherapy.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Suggest how you would use psychotherapy to help your patient to resolve his fear of women.

text: You are a practising psychotherapist and you know how to treat patients and the underlying causes
of disorders. One of your patients is a male who has a fear of women.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the biochemical explanation of schizophrenia.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Suggest how you would investigate whether the cause of schizophrenia is genetic or
biochemical. 
Psychology and Organisations
Section A
Answer this question.

text: There are various competing explanations of schizophrenia, one of which is the biochemical
explanation.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by the term ‘behavioural theory of leadership’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe two behavioural theories of leadership. 
Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have found out about motivation to work.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
We can motivate ourselves or the job can motivate us. Evaluate what psychologists have
found out about motivation to work and include a discussion of the issue of individual versus
situational explanations. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how you would measure job satisfaction in your organisation.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain the psychology on which your suggestion is based.

text: Workers in your organisation have a bad attitude towards work. Absenteeism is high and you need
to know why. You decide to give the workers a questionnaire with a rating scale to find out if their
bad attitude is related to poor job satisfaction.

parts.text: Suggest how bias might be avoided in personnel selection decisions.

parts.text:
Describe two personnel selection decision-making models.
